newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch says NZ monetary adjustment has taken place.
newsitem.headline: Birch says NZ monetary adjustment has taken place.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said in a speech on Thursday that the recent fall in value of the kiwi dollar, after a period in which it has been perceived as over-valued, seemed to have carried out an adjustment in monetary conditions desired by the Reserve Bank.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (the central bank) has wanted to see a rebalancing of monetary policy leading to higher interest rates and a lower exchange rate, Birch said.
"That adjustment now seems to have taken place, with the trade weighted exchange rate having fallen nearly six percent since mid-April," Birch said in the text of a speech.
At midday on Thursday the Trade Weighted Index (TWI) stood at 64.46, compared with about 68.75 on April 14.
Much of this fall has been concentrated in the last few weeks, when the TWI has dropped from just over 67 on June 26 in a sharp correction many in the market believed was overdue.
At the same time as this slide has taken place, 90-day bank bill rates have jerked sharply higher in a rebasing of market monetary conditions. Birch also commented on this trend.

"While the fall in the TWI has seen an upward movement in short-term interest rates, they are still considerably lower than 12 months ago and the Treasury, Reserve Bank, and independent commentators still estimate that the economy will begin to grow strongly again through the next three years," he told a business audience in Christchurch, South Island.
Birch repeated that the government remains confident of the prospects for a recovery in growth.

He said that along with easier overall monetary conditions, other factors underpinning growth would be increased government spending over the next year, the healthy state of the markets into which New Zealand exports, an anticipated pick-up in the price of some commodities and tax cuts.
He repeated that cuts beyond those scheduled for next year would be dependent on economic and fiscal conditions permitting.
